::: {#rem-quantifier-de-morgan}
#### De Morgan's laws for quantifiers

@thm-negate-quantifiers is often written
$\neg \forall x, P(x) \equiv \exists x, \neg P(x)$
and $\neg \exists x, P(x) \equiv \forall x, \neg P(x)$.
These notes say "has the same truth value" instead,
because $P(x)$ is a predicate, not a proposition,
so @def-logical-equivalence, which compares truth tables, does not apply.

On a finite set $S = \{a, b\}$,
$\forall x \in S, P(x)$ has the same truth value as $P(a) \land P(b)$,
and $\exists x \in S, P(x)$ has the same truth value as $P(a) \lor P(b)$,
so @thm-negate-quantifiers is De Morgan's laws (@thm-de-morgan-logic)
applied to $P(a)$ and $P(b)$.

Racket shows the same pattern on a list:
`(not (andmap even? (list 2 4 5)))` and `(ormap odd? (list 2 4 5))` both return `#t`.

:::
